q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a surgical mask?
title: Surgical mask carbon footprint per piece
short: Add the spunbond and meltblown polypropylene layers, nose wire and ear loops per mask with supplier figures. Add the mask machine electricity and packing, then divide by masks packed. Polypropylene fabric is most of the material.

ul: Nose wire and elastic ear loops.
Automatic mask machines with ultrasonic welding.

p: Report per mask and per box of fifty. Layers and fabric GSM decide most of the material.

example.title: Worked example: surgical mask unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 7,100 / 3,000,000 = 0.00237 kg CO2 per piece
Add nonwoven fabric and loops for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
